key_findings.finding_1: Active coordination documents (PLAN.md, README.md) and spec folders are well-organized and unambiguous
key_findings.finding_2: Five loose reports clearly map to their primary specs and contain evidence/findings for remediation
key_findings.finding_3: plans-reports-references.csv is accurate and comprehensive; it is the single source of truth for all relationships
key_findings.finding_4: No redundant or conflicting file structure discovered; spec folders contain only requirements/design/tasks
key_findings.finding_5: All loose reports contain explicit spec references; move is straightforward and low-risk
key_findings.finding_6: No repository scripts or active workflows depend on the root-level location of loose reports; move will not break automation

rationale: Loose reports are evidence documents that belong alongside their specs in a 'ref' (reference/evidence) subdirectory
The current root-level location of reports creates visual clutter and mixes active coordination documents with reference evidence
Moving reports to plans/ref aligns with repository conventions stated in README.md and AGENTS.md about document placement
The move is low-risk: only five files, clear spec relationships, minimal cross-references, and no script dependencies
After move, plans/ root level remains focused on active coordination: PLAN.md, README.md, adr/, six spec folders, one manifest CSV
plans/ref becomes the authoritative location for all audit reports, baseline documents, execution evidence, and verification records
